m1-span-hash.title: span_hash(node): a normalised, reformat-immune AST hash -- the atomic primitive, tested standalone before wiring
m1-span-hash.imperative: In scripts/code_map/extract.py add span_hash(node): ast.dump(node, annotate_fields=False) with the leading docstring Expr stripped (mutate node.body, dump, restore in a finally) so comment-and-prose-only edits don't count, then sha1-truncate. RED: write a standalone unit test (name containing 'stale_tag') that parses two source variants of the same function differing only in indentation/line-wrap/blank-lines/comments and asserts span_hash is EQUAL, plus a variant with a real body change (different return value or added statement) and asserts span_hash DIFFERS -- observe it fail (function does not exist yet), attest c1. GREEN: implement span_hash, make the test pass, attest c2 by running it.

postconditions.statement: TDD red: standalone span_hash test written and observed failing (function absent) -- manual attest
span_hash implemented; reformat-immunity and real-change-sensitivity both proven by the standalone test

m2-persist-and-diff.title: Persist span_hash on each anchored statement at extraction; on a second extraction of the same --artifacts dir, diff old vs new by slug and emit stale-anchor statements
m2-persist-and-diff.imperative: Wire span_hash into Extractor.anchor(): emit d={'span_hash': h} on every 'anchored' statement (the only authored-identity/tag-analog surface that exists pre-g7 -- comment tags land in g7 and will reuse the same [slug] allocator, so this is the correct hook point, stated as a decision, not assumed). In extract.run(), before overwriting statements.jsonl, read the PREVIOUS file's anchored statements (if any) into old_hashes[slug]=span_hash; after extracting, compare against new_hashes[slug]=(sym,hash) and append one 'stale-anchor' statement per slug present in both with a differing hash (bootstraps to nothing flagged when no previous store exists). RED: a test (name containing 'stale_tag') that runs extract twice on the same fixture+artifacts dir -- once unchanged/reformatted (expect NO stale-anchor row), once with a real body mutation on an anchored function (expect a stale-anchor row for that slug) -- observe it fail before the diff exists, attest c1. GREEN: implement, make it pass, attest c2.

m3-render-report.title: Surface stale-anchor statements in render_report.json (the run report) and as printed FAIL lines, without breaking the exit code (advisory, not build-breaking)
m3-render-report.imperative: In render.py's load_stores(), intercept p=='stale-anchor' explicitly (never let it fall into the edges/uses_lines catch-all -- add the branch right after the 'anchored' branch, same pattern) into a module-level stale_tags list (cleared in load_stores' reset loop). In render.run(), print one 'FAIL stale tag [slug]: ...' line per entry (same shape as the existing duplicate-id print) naming what a human should do (review the tag against the changed code; update or remove it), add report['stale_tags'] = [...ids...], and do NOT change the return code on stale tags alone (advisory -- unlike a duplicate id, a stale tag is not necessarily wrong, so failing the build on it would be exactly the twitchy tripwire the gb ruling warns against; state this reasoning in the code comment). RED: full-pipeline test(s) (names containing 'stale_tag', reusing/extending _make_anchor_repo the way IdsJsonlTests builds twice into the same --artifacts dir) -- build once, mutate ONLY a reformat (assert render_report.json['stale_tags'] empty, no FAIL line), build again with a real body mutation on an anchored function (assert the slug appears in render_report.json['stale_tags'] and in stdout) -- observe failing first, attest c1. GREEN: implement, make it pass, attest c2. Also assert render_report.json still carries no timing field (existing determinism constraint) and run the full determinism check unaffected.
